title: The pillars, reviewed
hookLine: five pillars, now understood from the inside

lines: FIVE WORDS ON AN INDEX CARD.
A LONG WHILE INSIDE EACH ONE.
cards: Five words fit on an index card: testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage. A visitor to a mosque could learn the list over one cup of tea. You met them on day nine, as a house built on five.

This year stayed a long while inside each one: the words of the testimony, the standing and bowing of the prayer, the arithmetic and the mercy of zakat, the long afternoons of the fast, the white cloth of the pilgrimage.
Now the year is closing, and these last days gather what it taught. First, the pillars, from the inside.

teach.h: BUILT ON FIVE: A HOUSE, NOT A LIST.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says Islam is built on five: bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, the pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan.
Built on: a house, not a checklist. Now each one from the inside. The testimony is said with the tongue, and Muslim teachers say it has to be meant: words that count when they're sincere.
The prayer: the Qur'an praises the believers "Who are humble in their prayers." Standing and bowing are the outside; that humility, khushu', is the inside.
Zakat: the Qur'an tells the Prophet to take alms from people's wealth to purify them, in paraphrase. The giving cleans the giver, not only feeds the poor.
The fast: in Pickthall's Qur'an, fasting is prescribed "that ye may ward off (evil)." The hunger is the outside; the guarding is the inside.
The pilgrimage: the Qur'an says the flesh and blood of the sacrifice don't reach Allah, but the devotion of the people does, in paraphrase.

teach.h: EACH PILLAR HAS A BODY AND A HEART.
teach.b: Each pillar has a body and a heart. In Muslim teaching, the body is required: the movements, the amounts, the days. And the texts keep pointing past the body to what it carries.
Not skipping the outside, but finding what it holds. And the pillars lean on each other.

teach.h: HUMBLE IN PRAYER, GUARDED IN THE FAST.
THE PILLARS LEAN ON EACH OTHER.
teach.b: The fast holds a month. The pilgrimage, for whoever is able, can hold a whole life.

how: Muslims keep the pillars as acts with set forms: saying the testimony, praying the daily prayers at their times, paying zakat on qualifying wealth, fasting the month of Ramadan, and making the Hajj if able; teachers stress the intention and humility behind each act.

o: five columns that hold up the dome of every mosque
the five Islam is built on, each with a body and a heart
five rules a convert must master before joining

games.q: the pillars, from the inside — tap the pairs.

s: the pillars are only outward rituals
the texts keep pointing inward: humility in prayer, purifying in zakat, guarding in the fast.
a hadith says Islam is built on five
Sahih al-Bukhari: the testimony, the prayer, zakat, the pilgrimage and the fast of Ramadan.
"from the inside" means the outward acts can be skipped
in Muslim teaching the body of each pillar is required; the inside is what it carries.

games.q: the time for prayer comes while you're in the middle of work. today's line is "from the inside." which fits it?
o: skip the prayer and just think kind thoughts.
pray, and let the movements carry humility.
pray as fast as possible and get back to work.
games.why: the Qur'an praises those "who are humble in their prayers": the body and the heart together, not one instead of the other.

practice: Bring to mind the next prayer of the day, the one coming after this lesson. If you pray, decide now where you'll be when it comes, and plan to stop for it when it arrives, not after.
If you don't, choose that same moment anyway, and when it comes, pause for one breath and remember that somewhere, someone is standing for that prayer just then.

wordCard.voice: The pillars. The five things Islam is built on, in the hadith's words: testimony, prayer, zakat, pilgrimage and fasting, each with a body and a heart. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: pillars; the five are called arkan al-islam, the pillars of Islam.

carryVoice: Your line: from the inside. The body of each pillar carries a heart. Until tomorrow.
